chunks: Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir who said:
The waiting period ('iddah) of the girl who has not yet reached menstruation is three months, and that of the woman who has ceased menstruation is three months.
We interpret this report as referring to a girl whose like would menstruate, because Allah the Exalted stipulated this and restricted it to one whose state is in doubt.

Allah the Exalted said: 'And those of you who die and leave wives — they shall wait for themselves four months and ten [days]; and those who have given up hope of menstruation among your women, if you doubt, then their waiting period is three months; and [also for] those who do not menstruate.'

He stipulated in the obligation of the three-month waiting period that she must be one in doubt; and thus was the meaning in His Exalted Saying: 'And those who do not menstruate,' meaning their waiting period is three months.
And this is preferable to what Ibn Sama'ah said, because he said the waiting period is obligatory upon all of these.
And the waiting period is dropped for the slave-girls, because this is a specification by him regarding slave-girls without evidence.
And what we mentioned is the view of Mu'awiyyah ibn Hakim, from the early jurists of our companions, and all our later jurists.
And it is consistent with the apparent meaning of the Quran, and we have fully explained the interpretation of what contradicts our ruling from the reports that came previously.
Therefore, there is no reason to repeat them.

key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: Waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a girl who has not yet started menstruating?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the 'iddah for pre-pubescent and post-menopausal women by linking the three-month period to the Quranic condition of 'doubt' (irtib), rather than applying it universally as Ibn Sama'a suggested. The text affirms the consensus of early and later Shia jurists, particularly Mu'awiyyah ibn Hakim, that this interpretation aligns with the apparent meaning of the Quran and resolves apparent contradictions in other reports.
